personas.name: The Paper-to-Digital Transitioner
personas.profile: Built a heating and cooling business using carbon-copy invoices. This fictional owner wants familiar, shallow navigation and clear confirmation while learning a new tool.
goals: Save business details without losing work
Find and follow up a quote request
context: Desktop at a busy service counter

personas.name: The High-Volume Mobile Dispatcher
personas.profile: Coordinates 15 trucks from a service vehicle and checks incoming homeowner enquiries on a small touch screen. Dispatch itself is outside the LeadQuote scope.
goals: Read quote details on a phone
Preview the quote experience with touch-sized controls

personas.name: The Office-Bound Operations Hawk
personas.profile: Co-owner working from an office desktop, focused on a fast, consistent setup and minimal repeated entry. Treat dispatch and billing-system automation as scope questions.
personas.business: Eight-truck HVAC company with an office team
goals: Recover cleanly from an entry mistake
Find a saved enquiry without unnecessary steps
context: Limited tolerance for duplicate data entry

personas.name: The Commercial Contract Estimator
personas.profile: Experienced commercial retrofit estimator exploring whether an instant-estimate price book fits the early enquiry stage. Multi-page proposals and arbitrary commercial line items are not assumed capabilities.
personas.business: Commercial and residential HVAC retrofit company
goals: Understand supported products and quote limitations
Review pricing controls on a tablet
Identify product-fit gaps without confusing them with defects

personas.name: The Micro-Business Solo Operator
personas.profile: Runs a one-person HVAC business, switches between customer calls and field work, and needs to resume setup without remembering previous inputs.
goals: Check what the homeowner will see
context: Phone during a break from attic work

limitations: Synthetic persona simulation and an engineering rubric, not research with real HVAC owners or a validated psychometric usability measure.
Timing is automation wall-clock time. Injected typing/thinking/wait delays are recorded separately; network and browser work remain included.
Glare, greasy hands, low battery and distraction are contextual hypotheses. Viewport, touch mode, pacing, network latency, throughput and explicit interruptions are the emulated conditions.
Visible completion does not establish backend persistence, email/SMS receipt, billing accuracy or provider delivery.
Automated accessibility checks are partial and do not certify WCAG conformance. Full keyboard, screen-reader and real-device checks remain necessary.

Blueprint adoption is page-referenced in docs/BLUEPRINT-PLAN.md. Current-view signals are heuristic observations; typography and field counts are not universal rules. Navigation/paint timings are lab samples, not a Core Web Vitals field assessment.
Text redaction is best effort; names, addresses and screenshots may contain sensitive data. Artifacts must stay private unless separately reviewed.
Blocked requests and stale selectors can affect findings. Reproduce observed issues in the approved current deployment before acting.
HTTP GET loading can have application-side effects on poorly designed targets. Browser request policy is not a server sandbox; use only an approved isolated tenant.
Fast mode disabled realistic pacing and latency; this run is a harness verification, not a field-condition timing run.
Published synthetic example omits screenshots; generate a fresh local demo for screenshot files.
